Hi Crystal / InkWear ops,

Thanks again for the sample run — the embroidered jackets and insulated pouches look great. We have one logistical wrinkle: several of the promotional kits include a gel cold pack and a small thermal liner to keep items under 15°C during day-of transport and short-term holding at the venue. Moscone's receiving team requires explicit handling instructions for temperature-sensitive materials.

Can you confirm the following by EOD Monday?
- Cold-pack freeze temp and thaw tolerance (we need SLA: must remain <=15°C for 8 hours after removal from freezer)
- Recommended palletization (single pallet vs mixed pallets) and max units per pallet for temperature maintenance
- Whether dry ice is required for our arrival window (we're aiming for day-of delivery 10/21, 07:00-09:00)

I attached the cold-pack spec sheet and the current packing manifest for reference. Lauren / Mina — looping you in to coordinate courier check-in and moves at the venue.

Thanks,

Hi Ben — thanks for the detailed note. Quick answers below and attached a handling guideline PDF for venue teams.

- Our 600g gel packs are specified to be refrigerated at -18°C for storage. Once thawed and activated, they maintain <=15°C for up to 10 hours in a standard insulated kit (lab test at ambient 20–25°C).
- For palletization we recommend single-product pallets: no more than 18 boxes per 48x40 pallet when the line items include gel packs and liners. Mixed pallets increase conductive heating risk.
- Dry ice is not required for the 07:00–09:00 arrival window provided kits are shipped with one pre-frozen pack per kit and insulated liners. If arrival slips beyond 4 hours we recommend adding phase-change liners or a dry ice layer.

We also attach a venue-facing PDF that lists labeling language Moscone requests. Please confirm final pallet counts and arrival slot so we can print the correct labels.

Regards,
Crystal Park
Client Ops — CoolShip Logistics
